as_told.title: Analysis of the Roswell piece finds sub-wavelength waveguide channels

plain: A metal piece made of thin layers of bismuth and magnesium, said to come from the 1947 Roswell crash in New Mexico, contains tiny channels for guiding waves, far smaller than the waves themselves. The physicist Hal Puthoff says he checked the piece himself and found these miniaturized channels, which he calls quite an accomplishment. Jesse Michels, relaying what Puthoff told him, adds that the material could shrink such channels for terahertz waves, a very high radio frequency, though Puthoff in his own telling does not mention terahertz.
